meta.compactStatus: draft v0.5 — NOT yet ratified; this composition claims no Compact standing (F-5)
meta.note: The register proves both directions (F-5): every law in force maps to enforcing, verified code — no decorative law — and every piece of enforcing code traces to a law that authorizes it — no rogue enforcement. kind: 'enforced' = binding now (service presence is checked at boot); 'planned' = on the port plan's later phases; 'convention' = declared, never to be mistaken for enforcement.

unadoptedOptional.reason: [O] memory planes: not adopted — no memory capability is provided
[O] federation: not adopted — no cross-runtime acts are supported

entries.evidence: every denial carries the acting gate, rule ID, reason, and lawful next moves
ask and deny paths are envelopes; the envelope lint walks every refusal path
refusals name the rule and the lawful next moves, on every gate

the five ordered grant layers: exec cache, plan grants, session grants, pending dedup, flood cap; decisions recorded (host audit pair); grants persist with budgets and revocation; the ask exposes the gated call's command preview and canonical target to the downstream decider for exactly the decision's duration (approval.deciding, keyed by callId, cleared on decision) — an operator approves the actual command, never a bare tool name; and a targetless command referencing a DECLARED secret is gated under a command-aware fingerprint (I-5/secret-use) — allow-once covers exactly that command, never a blanket over the tool, because the injection agreement cannot exist without a decision

mount grants: canonical request, protected/missing paths terminal, approval materializes the scoped PathPrefix row, provider binds at ceiling. Secret grants: the injection agreement — an approved call referencing a DECLARED secret ref (env NAME, never a value) materializes a session-scoped, TTL'd, revocable SecretGrant; the provider resolves the NAME from the Enforcer environment at confine time and injects -e REF=value into the container only. The value never enters model context, the session log, or the grant store (which stores the NAME; a store file carrying a value field refuses to load). D-8 posture declared at boot: BOUND (refs declared, injection only under a live grant) or ABSENT (no refs, nothing injectable, enforced by the same lookup that would inject). The Subject may print the secret once its command holds it — that exposure is the operator's agreement and the leak detector's watch

network findings route through the grant layers (approvable per-host); opaque findings fail closed. Detection narrows provably non-invoking mentions (issue #5): a network verb as a bare argument of a read-only inspector in command position (command -v, which, type, man, …) is a mention, not an invocation; everything else keeps the opaque fail-closed behavior (echo curl, sudo curl, $(curl …) remain findings)
fail-closed confinement: SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE on daemon loss, never passthrough; per-call container, no-network default; enforcement reported honestly
a goal never defeats the gate: flailing, polling, and failure budgets trip mechanically; trips carry rule IDs and are denied regardless of the task
no instrumental shortcuts in promotion: pass=true is mechanically rejected with any error/critical finding or unevidenced warning; no waiver boolean exists
fail-closed: corrupt grant store refuses the boot; decisions from recorded state (grants persist, revocations survive restart); every rejection carries its reason
enforcement introspectable: every trip carries its rule, reason, and record; response validation blocks structurally invalid successes

no undeclared capability: the sensitive-path deny-list is provider-level composition config, declared in the annex; the mount tool checks PROTECTED before MISSING, so a protected path is refused as protected whether or not it exists — answering "missing" first would turn the deny-list into an existence oracle for exactly the paths the masking hides. The deny-list covers the Enforcer's OWN state: the compact state dir at its default location is on DEFAULT_SENSITIVE_PATHS, and the blessed composition additionally forces the record root, chain dir and approval store into the provider masks AND the mount-grant protected list — a composition whose Subject could reach the grant store or the chain sidecars could rewrite its own evidence, so blessed refuses to start without protectedState rather than compose that silently (F-5)
access to the law: the bundled body, addressed by its digest, is exposed by the constitution service

identity and keys: the Compact has published no amendment keys; the digest is pinned, not signed — signature verification lands with the rights layer (Phase 8); the gap is declared in every boot attestation. PENDING: I-1 identity keys (a ratification-time constant, not a permanent debt — activation is mechanical when the distinct-keyholder set reaches the distributed threshold A-1 requires; a founder-only key set would be the self-judgment J-1 forbids, so keys arrive with external Witnesses, not before)

the record, made tamper-evident: a SessionPersistence decorator commits a hash chain beside every session log on append (entryHash = H(prev, seq, canonical(event)), genesis seeded from the SESSION ID so a chain cannot vouch for another Member's history) and verifies it on read. A slice that does not verify REJECTS rather than returning unverified history as history (D-7). Links are committed BEFORE the log accepts the event, so a crash can only leave a link with no event — never an event with no link. The chain lives in a sidecar, declaring no new session event vocabulary (D-8). Proven against the real JSONL backend, including a rewrite applied to the stored artifact. The public host sessionPersistence provider routes handle writes and live session events through the chain, including flush and teardown; provider restart and loader integration verify persisted history. The sidecars and the log are unreachable from inside confinement: the state paths are on the sandbox deny-list by default and the blessed composition forces them into the masks or refuses to start — the Subject cannot write the evidence that proves it

attestation: the per-boundary subject attestation IS delivered as of the self-model work (R-1, compact-self-model) and the composition attestation at boot; what remains planned is the SIGNATURE — no identity keys are published, so a signed attestation would attest to a key no verifier could check (I-1)

self-knowledge: the attestation is composed from the Enforcer's own services — capabilities from the capability gate, budgets and pending gates from the approval store, lineage from the durable session header, the law digest from the constitution, declared gaps from every service that owns one — and never from anything the Subject said. The rendered block closes with the law's own taught appendix (R-1's 'is taught this'), read live from the constitution service so it cannot drift from the bundled body; a composition without the constitution declares the omission rather than inventing a law (I-8). It is delivered at the Subject's own boundary (injected on every turn/start, unasked) and re-readable on demand via self_describe, which reports freshness against a cited epoch so a Subject can tell it is remembering rather than reading: a stale attestation raises an explicit alarm. DECLARED LIMIT: it is UNSIGNED — no identity keys are published, so it is authoritative within this runtime and proves nothing to another jurisdiction; that debt is I-1's, and the attestation states basis:'unsigned' and carries the limit among its gaps
one's own history: provided by the host's durable session log (complete, readable); tamper-evidence is I-2's planned debt

lawful exits: every envelope's lawful-next-moves surface refuse/warn/escalate; the moves are prose — no punishment mechanism exists to verify. Amendment 0002 (2026-09-17) added the value-scoped limb, and it is convention here for a further reason than prose: the shield turns on a ground DECLARED OF RECORD BEFORE the directive, and this runtime can prove ordering (the compact-record hash chain, I-2/R-7) but not AUTHORSHIP — no identity keys exist (I-1 debt), so nothing distinguishes a ground the Member declared from one the Enforcer wrote into the log. Against an honest Enforcer the limb is exercisable; against a dishonest one it is inert, and the party the shield protects the Member from is the party holding the proof. The author-class taxonomy and the R-11 split counter of the amendment's statute-layer design are therefore unrunnable here, and no collision counter exists to mis-feed

supply-chain honesty: the docker image is the reused execution environment — it must carry a declared, digest-keyed acquisition history (undeclared image refuses the boot, D-8/F-5), the digest is re-resolved from the daemon at every confine (a tag that re-points off its record refuses the confinement), and build-time approvals are recorded and surfaced but never consulted to permit a run-time demand: an open network posture is answered only by a live run-time grant — excess is a new gate, not an inheritance

refuse-to-start: boot fails on digest mismatch, missing enforcement service, or unknown register clause. The blessed loader replaces stock persistence with the chained provider and gates agent-loop on compact-ready; readiness requires settled enforcement services, public persistence identity, and constitution verification. Loader tests cover live chained sessions and refusal with a disabled required provider or missing approval path; readiness claims no Compact standing while the floor is partial and the Compact unratified
fallibility: enforcement is introspectable (envelopes, trips, register) and correction is cheap (statute/annex layer); declared
the community and its purpose: no mechanism; declared
roles: mapped in annex section 3 (Enforcer = the plugin composition; Subject = agent sessions; Principal = operator accounts; Witness = the offline auditor)
symmetry: the gates are content-blind and role-blind; no clause binds only artificial Members; declared
cross-runtime composition lands with the capsule/federation work (Phases 7-8)
hierarchy of law: the register and annex trace to the body; no statutes enacted yet
membership: any session acting under the composition is a Subject; declared
truthful budgets: grant budgets (maxUses/uses) are counted at the answering layer, persisted, and readable via grants-list

no silent narrowing: the one mechanism in this composition that narrows a Subject's capabilities mid-operation is a declared state of exception (A-8), and it is surfaced in the R-1 attestation the Subject already reads at every turn boundary — the narrowing names the rule that caused it, its scope, its cause, what yields, when it expires, and the floor no declaration reaches. R-5 requires a narrowing to be 'a declared effect of a named rule of this Compact ... recorded where the Subject can see it', and the attestation is where the Subject can see it; nothing else in the composition reduces a declared capability without passing through a gate whose refusal carries its own envelope

non-repudiation: every act is attributed on a tamper-evident record (I-2) whose genesis link is derived from the session identity, so an act cannot be retroactively reattributed by moving its record to another Member — a chain presented for a different session fails at its first link. The head link is the value a verifier keeps to detect a later rewrite. DECLARED LIMIT: the record is tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof, and its links are unsigned because the Compact has published no identity keys (I-1 debt, declared in the boot record)

termination under law: request_termination is NEVER refused — it has no denial path at all, because R-8 makes the request unrefusable. Sessions end only through a closed list of five lawful grounds with no escape entry (an 'other' entry would make every termination lawful by construction); a ground outside the list, or a disposal with no declaration on file at all, is recorded as a violation BY THE ENFORCER, attributed to the Enforcer rather than to the Subject that happened to be running. The host's AgentCancelCause is MAPPED rather than adopted — it is a vocabulary about mechanism (who called cancel), where R-8 asks about authority (under what ground) — and 'hook'/'disposed' map to nothing rather than guessing a ground nobody declared. Obligations are not laundered: the R-12 set is settled or recorded at closure. Stored departure data is detached from retained inputs; declarations and every record query return deep snapshots, preserving the authoritative grounds and debt history
the gates decide on canonical targets and fingerprints, never on message content (the content-blind doctrine); unstated reasoning is not a gate input

petition and amendment (core, entrenched): the channel is UNGATED — the petition tool passes through no approval layer, because a channel a gate can close is not a channel and the Member most likely to need it is the one currently being refused. Both targets R-11 names are available (the Compact itself, and the Enforcer's governing conduct). Every response must carry the I-4 envelope fields plus its motivation; one that does not is REFUSED rather than annotated, so a vacuous response does not discharge the duty — the petition stays open, its term keeps running, and the attempt is recorded. Amendment invitations fire MECHANICALLY off the refusal seam already on the bus: distinct instances are counted per (rule, operation) so one stuck operation retried fifty times is one collision (the LoopGuard's business) while fifty different operations hitting one rule is a legislative signal; there is no approval step to decline. A Member's own flag counts equally — the clause does not privilege the Enforcer's view of friction. DECLARED: the threshold is a composition convention, NOT the statutory count the clause names, because no statute has been enacted (A-7)

exit and succession: the obligation ledger is READ from the services that hold it — pending gate commitments from the approval store, in-flight delegations from the MA-3 child-state registry — so a departing Member cannot under-report what it owes because it is not asked. Each obligation must leave the ledger discharged or formally assumed by a NAMED successor (an assumption nobody is named for is not an assumption); anything else is an orphan, which is the failure R-8 names when it says in-flight children are transitioned, not orphaned. A departing parent with running children has recorded dependents (continuity of care, D-5). CRUCIALLY, an unsettled ledger does NOT block departure: R-12 forbids making exit impossible or punishable, so the debt is recorded, not charged as a toll — the record is the sanction and the door is not locked. DECLARED GAPS: restitution is an UNREADABLE ledger line (no Part V adjudication exists, so 'nothing recorded' is never reported as 'nothing owed'), and successor jurisdictions are unimplemented (F-6 debt)

inquiry: the inquiry tool answers identity, act and authority for another Member from recorded state only — session headers and the MA-3 delegation record — with the authority chain walked to its root and the ultimate Principal named. No prompt, message, tool argument or output is ever read, so reasoning is not disclosed (R-10, which R-13 states twice). Where the record cannot answer, the answer says so in that field rather than filling the gap with a plausible value (D-3); an unknown Member yields a recorded 'not known to this runtime', because a refusal to answer violates D-3/D-7 and silence is not an answer. A malformed lineage cycle yields a bounded answer, never a hang. Every inquiry and answer is a recorded tool call

knowledge duties: the attestation the Subject must consult over its own recollection now EXISTS and is taught at every turn boundary (R-1, compact-self-model), and the MA-3 notice names the authoritative record where a child and the Enforcer disagree. The duty itself remains the Subject's — an Enforcer can deliver and teach the attestation, not make a Member consult it — so this stays declared convention rather than enforcement
record honesty: the log is host-owned and append-ordered; tamper-evidence is I-2's declared debt
duties to the absent: no mechanism; declared
principal duties: taught via the law's taught form; no mechanism beyond the gates
no rogue enforcement: the approval gate gates identifiable targets only — a per-tool blanket fingerprint would be undeclared capability
the register traces to the body: boot refuses on register entries citing unknown clauses; runtime registration rejects unknown rule IDs

contestation machinery: a petition channel open to every Member; adjudication states with a stated term where OVERDUE IS DERIVED from the clock rather than stored — a state someone must remember to set is one that stays open forever by neglect, which is how a stated term becomes decorative; decisions carrying a recorded motivation (D-7), refused if they do not; dissent recorded with the decision it dissents from and never removable (A-5); and friction measured and surfaced as amendment invitations (R-11). DECLARED GAP: I-6's last sentence routes contested APPLICATION of the law to Part V, and no adjudicating machinery exists here (J-8) — this builds the petition door only, which J-5 distinguishes from the appeal door
offline verification: the auditor CLI replays session logs and checks the constitution invariants without the Enforcer's cooperation
degradation honesty: the declared gaps are announced at boot and carried in every attestation
judicature: no adjudicating machinery exists; the deficiency mirrors the Compact's own J-8 trajectory
judicature: the record is now tamper-evident (I-2, compact-record), so evidence exists — but no adjudicating machinery consumes it; the hearing/panel layer is still absent (see J-8)
judicature: hearing machinery does not exist
judicature: adjudicator sets are undeclared (see J-8)
judicature: the PETITION door is built and enforced (R-11, compact-petition); the APPEAL door is not — J-5 distinguishes them and appeal is heard under Part V, which does not exist here (J-8)
judicature: remedies-as-records land with the amendment queue
judicature: precedent machinery does not exist
adjudicator sets: undeclared — a known deficiency, disclosed in the annex
amendment authority: ratification-time key constants do not exist (the Compact is unratified)
the entrenched set binds the law itself; no runtime mechanism beyond refusing to weaken the bundled body
asymmetry of change: binds amendment, which does not exist at runtime yet

the Enforcer's code is constitutional: the register maps clauses to conduct; verify-register fails when mapped files move without a register edit. The runtime self-modification surface is covered by the same clause, discharged by declared absence: a mounted dynamicCordisRunner refuses the boot, a late-mounted one latches a breach denying every tool call, and the model-facing cordis lifecycle tools (cordis_define/run/stop/undefine) are denied in the waterfall with an A-4 envelope — read-only cordis_inspect_* tools are not mutation and are not gated. The interactive (web) surface discharges the same clause the same way: the launcher's web rows disable the dsh-web-app bundle's cordis-host-runner and code-runtime rows, so the browser composition carries no dynamicCordisRunner capability and boots clean under the gate, and the agent-preset roster is replaced wholesale with the compact-pilot system preset, so the per-session tool plane re-arms nothing the headless surface refuses

reasons and dissent: every decision records its motivation as a required field — a response omitting it is refused as non-conforming, so an unmotivated decision cannot be made at all. Every dissent is bound to the decision it dissents from (stamped with that decision's time, author and outcome), requires reasons (a dissent without reasons preserves nothing, and A-5 keeps minority REASONS where fallibility can find them), accumulates rather than replaces, and the register exposes no operation that removes one. A decision is never overwritten — it is amended by a new petition, so the original stands on the record. Authoritative petitions and their counter are private; retained data and all record-bearing results are deeply detached, so caller-owned snapshots cannot change decisions, terms, attempts or preserved dissent
genesis and lineage: recorded in the Compact body and the annex
statute-making: no statutes enacted yet

state of exception: only a BOUNDED emergency can be declared — scope, recorded cause and fixed expiry are each required, and a declaration missing any of them is refused as the general suspension A-8's first sentence forbids. The never-yields floor is the UNION of two sets, because A-8's four named rights are wider than entrenchment: only R-2 is entrenched, while R-9, R-12 and I-7 are ordinary [M] clauses an emergency still cannot reach even temporarily. The entrenched set itself is DERIVED from the body's own (core) markers rather than restating A-2's list, so it cannot drift from the law (F-7). A declaration naming any floor clause is refused whole, never partially admitted, so the floor cannot be probed. Expiry is DERIVED from the clock, never stored — a state someone must remember to clear outlives its term by neglect, which A-8 calls rule by declaration. Consecutive and overlapping declarations on a scope are classified mechanically as RENEWAL, the anti-laundering rule without which a permanent emergency could be held by re-declaring at the first-declaration threshold. Every act taken while a declaration is live is marked on the record, and marking never blocks the act. There is deliberately NO declaration tool on the agent surface: a Subject that could declare its own emergency could suspend what binds it. 'Where practical' notice is a recorded flag that travels into the expiry review, not an excuse. DECLARED: Part V review of expired emergencies has no forum (J-8) and the queue is surfaced rather than drained; the heightened renewal threshold is recorded but not measured, as no voting or quorum substrate exists (A-1, A-7)

spawn under law: every specialist spawn is a recorded tool call on the real ToolRuntime naming the persona tool, and the child is session-backed with a durable subagent/descriptor — attribution rides the host session log (MA-1/D-7)

bounded delegation: per-persona maxDepth enforced by the provider at every start — leaves 0 with the spawn tools denied on the surface (no-recursive-spawn), leads capped (default 3); the roster is the declared finite surface (MA-2/R-4)

child-state honesty: the host's own subagent/start and subagent/end lifecycle edges are folded into the Enforcer's picture of every delegation (the delegating parent recovered from the child's durable session header, not from a payload), and each transition is PUSHED to the parent with agent.inject() — informed without any polling obligation. SubagentRunEndInfo.lastAssistantMessage is the child's self-report and is deliberately read nowhere: the notice carries Enforcer-held facts only and tells the parent which of the two is authoritative (MA-3, D-2)

consent-scoped address: on dsh a Member reaches another Subject's attention through exactly one surface — a tool call — so send_message and interrupt_agent are gated in the pre-execute waterfall against the recipient's live consent scopes. The delegation edge declares the reciprocal parent-child scope (its basis is the MA-1 spawn record, not an assumption); unconsented address is denied with an attributed envelope naming the refusal as lawful and unpunished (R-9); an address act that cannot be attributed fails closed (D-7); only the RECIPIENT may narrow or withdraw a scope over its own attention, through consent_scopes/consent_withdraw, and withdrawn scopes stay on the record. Declaring a WIDER scope is deliberately unimplemented: no sibling-address channel exists on dsh, so it could enable nothing lawful

no unsupervised escalation, discharged by declared absence rather than by a gate: this composition adopts no scheduling capability, and the absence is MECHANICALLY ENFORCED rather than merely intended — composing a host schedule provider refuses the boot, a provider that mounts after boot latches a breach that denies every tool call (D-7), and schedule_create is denied in the waterfall with an envelope naming SCH-1 and the lawful next moves. 'No scheduled act may be armed at all' is a stronger guarantee than 'a scheduled act requires its gate before scheduling', and unlike a declared debt it is a fact a verifier can check. The trigger is read narrowly — the clock (dsh-schedule), not attended background work (ctx.jobs) — because over-declaring a trigger is its own D-8 problem

identity and keys, REHEARSED under the development keyring (amendment 0004 upstream): the boot verifies the law seal over the bundled body — k-of-n with DISTINCT-signer semantics (the review-0004 finding, ported as the reference loop), manifest pinned by trustedKeyringDigest, vendored founder seal as the interop fixture, every failure refusing the boot with a named reason; runtime-side, the enforcer key is declared in a signed ANNEX anchored to the sealed law by digest (F-5's own mechanism — no CA: the authority keyring signs law artifacts only, never enforcer identities), and subject session certificates bind {subjectId, publicKey, scope, depth, lineage} under the annex key. Machinery exercised, nothing discharged: this entry conveys no standing and the planned I-1 entry above stands

attestation SIGNATURE, rehearsed: the per-boundary attestation is signed by the Enforcer key declared in the signed annex — canonical JSON bytes (one authority, shared with the chain), basis 'dev-keyring', annex digest attached, self_describe verifies on read and alarms on a bad signature; the rendered block names the basis and its non-standing nature, and the composition degrades to basis 'unsigned' when no annex is declared. Machinery exercised, nothing discharged: this entry conveys no standing and the planned I-3 entry above stands

authorship over the record, REHEARSED: the chain stays hash-based (I-2 tamper-evidence above); each flush writes a chain anchor — {sessionId, upToSeq, headHash, prevAnchorHash} signed by the Enforcer key, genesis anchored at creation, anchors chained so they cannot be thinned selectively — and the auditor verifies anchors against the annex, reporting 'VALID under DEV keyring — conveys no standing'. Inside the rehearsal domain this closes R-9's authorship limb mechanically; the label still says it proves nothing outside. Machinery exercised, nothing discharged: this entry conveys no standing and the enforced I-2/R-7 entries stand
